subject.title: [Bug] WebChat: optimistic USER messages are lost (not just hidden) when chat.send returns before the durable transcript lands — full-replace history reconcile drops them

question: Should WebChat `chat.send` ACK only after the user turn is durably recorded or progressing, or should the UI remain responsible for preserving optimistic sends while delayed runtime persistence stays allowed?
rationale: Current source and the open candidate PR show this is no longer a simple UI merge bug; the remaining fix changes the gateway/runtime durability contract and duplicate-suppression boundary.

options.title: Require Durable ACK
options.body: Adopt a gateway contract where WebChat `chat.send` succeeds only after the user turn is durably visible or scheduled with an auditable failure path.

options.title: Keep UI-Only Preservation
options.body: Treat current UI pending-send preservation as sufficient and leave delayed runtime-owned persistence as accepted behavior.

options.title: Replace Candidate PR
options.body: Close or supersede the broad gateway PR and ask for a narrower current-main design around the shared recorder/session-accessor boundary.

recommendation.title: Require Durable ACK
recommendation.body: Adopt a gateway contract where WebChat `chat.send` succeeds only after the user turn is durably visible or scheduled with an auditable failure path.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice centers on the shared user-turn recorder/session-accessor contract, which this history most directly connects to shakkernerd.
